newsitem.title: USA: Raytheon plans to issue $2.5 bln debt.
newsitem.headline: Raytheon plans to issue $2.5 bln debt.

text.p: Raytheon Co said on Thursday it planned to offer $2.5 billion of debt off its shelf registration statement during the first week of August.
Proceeds would be used to refinance Raytheon's recent acquisition of the defense systems and electronics business of Texas Instruments Inc, it said.
Marketing for the issue would start August 4, with the pricing of the securities expected later in the week, it said.
Raytheon said it planned to issue debt securities with final maturities of five, ten and 30 years.
The offering would be joint-lead managed by Credit Suisse First Boston, Morgan Stanley Dean Witter and Bear, Stearns & Co Inc, the company said.
Morgan Stanley would act as book running lead manager.
Raytheon is an high technology company operating in four business areas -- commercial and defense electronics, engineering and construction, aircraft and major appliances.
